 CT credit union signs endorsement deal with UConn’s Braylon Mullins
 UConn men's basketball player Braylon Mullins has signed an NIL endorsement deal with East Hartford-based Finex Credit Union. Contributed Photo 
 By David Krechevsky 
 November 4, 2026 
 Share 
 Copy URL Email Facebook X Linkedin 
 If you’re a credit union looking to promote “delivering in the clutch,” who better to symbolize that than last year’s author of “The Shot” during March Madness.
 East Hartford-based Finex Credit Union announced Wednesday it has signed an endorsement deal with Braylon Mullins of the UConn men’s basketball team.
 Mullis, a 6-foot-6 sophomore shooting guard from Indiana, hit the clutch, 35-foot game-winning shot with 0.3 seconds left against rival Duke in the NCAA Tournament’s Elite Eight to send UConn to the Final Four for the third time in four years.
 Finex said the endorsement deal with Mullins is intended to help promote the credit union’s commitment to helping members succeed.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
 Under the NCAA’s name, image and likeness (NIL) rules, college athletes can sign endorsement deals in addition to being paid by the school they attend.
 Joe Bartolotta, president and CEO of Finex, said the credit union has a great story to tell, “but sometimes you need someone special to help spread the word. We decided that no one better symbolizes that commitment to delivering in the clutch than Braylon.”
 Under the deal, Mullins will help emphasize the benefits of belonging to a member-owned financial institution, the credit union said. He will be featured in advertising across social media and streaming services, and make personal appearances during the basketball season, Finex said.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Founded in 1938, Finex Credit Union serves more than 16,000 members and manages more than $133 million in assets. In addition to East Hartford, it has branches in Vernon and Wallingford.
